clue.text: Wistful, locating characters out side society

indicators.note: outside says the shuffled letters go around the abbreviation for society
the characters of the word locating are taken and set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone feels wistful while hunting out people who live on the edge of society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' is the anagram signal: the characters of 'locating' are shuffled, and 'outside' puts them round the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a sentimental longing for the past or for something lost.

explanation.surface: Is music made famous by being music?
explanation.definitionFit: Illustrious people are famous ones; music written down is set out in notes, so it is literally furnished with them.

explanation.surface: Laundry starch has somehow ended up in a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is something that makes fabric rigid; a stiff tot of spirits is a slang term for a bracing drink.

clue.text: Bill, given sauce, needs dealing with

parts.note: a bill is an advertisement or poster, abbreviated AD
a salad dressing is a kind of sauce

explanation.surface: A restaurant bill that includes a charge for sauce has to be sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackling a problem or attending to a matter is a way of handling it.

clue.text: Bacon seen here perhaps, right inside kitchen

indicators.note: inside says the abbreviation for right is put within the word for a ship's kitchen

parts.note: a galley is the kitchen on a ship or aircraft

explanation.surface: Bacon frying in the kitchen, with something placed right inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' looks like breakfast, but it is Francis Bacon, the painter, whose work hangs in art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: An art museum is where paintings by an artist such as Francis Bacon are exhibited.

clue.text: Detailed body into which African leader's invested capital

indicators.note: invested means placed within, so one letter goes inside the shortened body
de-tailed means the last letter of the word for a dead body is cut off

parts.note: a carcass is a dead body

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A detailed corpse into which an African chief has put his money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as 'thorough' but means de-tailed: CARCASS loses its last S to give CARCAS, and 'invested' puts A (African's leader) inside it. Caracas is the capital of Venezuela.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracas is the capital city of Venezuela.

explanation.surface: Someone bungles the making of a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: To botch or cobble something together is one sense; the other is a soft toffee-like confection.

clue.text: Informer made to consider in common parlance?

indicators.note: in common parlance points to a working-class London pronunciation in which the th sound becomes f

parts.note: to consider is to think

explanation.surface: An informer is forced to reflect, in everyday speech.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney speech (London working-class dialect) 'th' is often said as 'f', so 'think' comes out as 'fink'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fink is American slang for a snitch or someone who tells tales to the authorities.

indicators.note: short means the final letter of the word for a simple song is cut off

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A brief song starts up once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same thing repeated, as said once more.

explanation.surface: The letter E stands for a remarkable display.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter E opens the word for the organ of sight; a startling revelation is the other sense.

indicators.note: negotiating suggests one thing getting through another, so the single letter goes into the jazz word

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single

explanation.surface: Jazz players working out a deal over a single set of three.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a group of three, as a triplet is.

clue.text: Glasses — fifty, alternatively, ten get drunk

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
or is a word offering an alternative

indicators.note: drunk means the words ten and get are jumbled

explanation.surface: Glasses: fifty, or else ten, get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held up on a handle.

explanation.surface: A change in a row of items.
explanation.definitionFit: Change in a sum is what is left over after subtraction; a row here is a quarrel, a disagreement.

clue.text: Where chickens sound like other birds, quiet

parts.note: pigeons and doves coo
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Chickens imitating other birds, but softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen house is the enclosure where poultry are kept.

clue.text: Composer has driven me to arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement, as in music, means the letters of the preceding words are reordered

explanation.surface: A composer has pushed me towards writing an arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Monteverdi was an Italian composer of early opera.

clue.text: Powerful family's time heartless and unpleasant

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the time word is removed

parts.note: a day is a period of time
nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A ruling family's era, cruel and disagreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of rulers or an influential family across generations.

parts.note: to deck someone is to knock them down
cha is tea

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over an Irish drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is a slang word for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding beach seat is the thing described as collapsible.

clue.text: Japanese leader confiscating Turkish leader's weapon

indicators.note: confiscating means taking something in, so the first letter goes inside the Japanese ruler

parts.note: a shogun was a military ruler of Japan

indicators.note: a leader is a word's first letter

explanation.surface: A Japanese ruler seizes a Turkish leader's firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a gun firing a spread of pellets.

clue.text: So a sliding effect doesn't have one? It is one!

indicators.note: effect is read as bring about, so the remaining letters are worked into a new form
doesn't have means a letter is dropped from the three opening words

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sliding musical effect without a glide? It is one!
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't have one' removes an I from SOASLIDING, and 'effect' rearranges the rest. The clue itself is also a description: a glissando is a sliding effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid slide between notes, which is a sliding effect in music.

clue.text: One presiding over inquest gains nothing during recess

indicators.note: gains means the recess word takes a letter into itself

parts.note: a corner is a recess or nook
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A judge at an inquest earns nothing in the break.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is the official who holds inquests into sudden deaths.

parts.note: a boxing match is fought in rounds
up means ahead, leading

explanation.surface: Gather round the boxing match leader?
explanation.definitionFit: To round up is to herd together or collect.

indicators.note: cracked means the letters of Detroit are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: More nuts come out of a city cracked open.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty means crazy, and nuts is slang for crazy.

indicators.note: to embrace means the sad word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: drear means dismal, sad

explanation.surface: An idealist, sad, wants to hug me.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary who hopes for a better world is a romantic idealist.

clue.text: In which guys used to be effeminate

definitions.text: In which guys used to be

explanation.surface: Where men used to be effeminate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guys' are the guy ropes of a tent, not men.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp of tents is held up by guy ropes; camp also describes exaggerated, effeminate behaviour.

parts.note: a mother, ma, is a relation
a son is a relation

explanation.surface: One putting up relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a builder working in stone.

parts.note: super means excellent
a visor is protection for the face or eyes

explanation.surface: A boss requires first-rate safety gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor is the manager who oversees workers.

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to bank on is to rely
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Carrying an item into the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay is to pass along or transmit, as a message is carried on.

indicators.note: it's reported signals a word that is heard rather than written

parts.note: bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Lots of girls drink, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: BEVVY is British slang for a drink, especially beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group, traditionally used of girls or women.

clue.text: City trades freely during a year of supposed computer failure

indicators.note: during means the rearranged letters sit inside the other pieces

parts.note: the millennium bug was feared to crash computers in 2000, MM in Roman numerals

indicators.note: freely means the letters of trades are rearranged at will

explanation.surface: A city where trading flowed freely during the millennium bug scare.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'supposed computer failure' was the millennium bug of 2000, MM in Roman numerals; 'freely' shuffles 'trades' and 'during' sets it between those Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital city of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Giving some children alcohol a sort of failure

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Giving children alcohol risks a kind of collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes RENAL from 'childREN ALcohol'; renal failure is kidney failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means of the kidneys, so it describes one sort of organ failure.

parts.note: the outermost letters of rampancy, its first and last, joined by the word and, spell the answer

explanation.surface: Aroused, displaying the height of unbridled lust.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'rampancy' are R and Y, which read as a phrase give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is British slang for lustful or sexually excited.

parts.note: par is a standard level
simony is the crime of buying or selling church offices

explanation.surface: A typical crime: being mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony means meanness with money, extreme thrift.
